Pushkar Hira S/o Sh. Pramod Kumar R/o H.No. 19, Maishih Garh, Sukhdev Vihar, New Delhi. ............Driver-cum-Owner/Respondent no. 1 2. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.. F-14 & 20 C.P. Circus, New Delhi. .........Insurance Company/Respondent no. 2 Date of accident : 22.10.2018 Date of filing of Dar : 07.01.2019 Date of Decision : 25.08.2022 Mact No. 05/19 Smt. Roshan Aara v. texts.facts: Compensation case regarding injury to Smt. Roshan Aara D/o Abdul Bahir Khan with 80 % permanent disability in relation to her right upper limb and both lower limb Award 1. In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 22.10.2018 at about 6 pm, petitioner was going on foot from her office to residence. When petitioner reached at Ma Anandmai Marg, Okhla Bus Stand, Phase-I, New Delhi and crossed the road, suddenly one vehicle bearing no. DL-3S-DV-3705 came at high speed and in rash manner and hit the petitioner forcefully and received grievous injuries. Smt. Roshan Aara vs Pushkar Hira on 25 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191802696/ 1 3. Injured was removed to ESI hospital where his MLC bearing no. 378/18 dated 22.10.2018 was prepared. Further, he took treatment from Holy Family hospital. He also received permanent disability. 4. Further, Medical Board of Pt. Madan Mohan Hospital, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi sent disability report dated 12.04.2022 noticing 80% permanent physical impairment in relation to right upper limb and both lower limb. 5. An FIR bearing No. 447/18 u/s 279,338 IPC PS Okhla Industrial Area, New Delhi was registered in this case. 6. In response to DAR, respondent No.1 driver-cum-owner and insurance company/respondent no.2 filed reply. 7. In reply filed by driver-cum-owner, it is in nutshell stated that he MACT No. 05/19 Smt. Roshan Aara v. Pushkar Hira Page No. 2 of 24 did not cause the accident in question. He further claimed that IO has filed a manipulated DAR. It is further claimed that he was driving the vehicle diligently. It is further stated that offending vehicle in question was duly insured. It is further claimed that he has a valid driving licence to drive the offending vehicle in question. As such, it is claimed that liability if any is of insurance company only. 8. In nutshell, in reply filed by insurance company in question, it is stated that the driving licence of the driver in question was not valid to drive the motorcycle and as such, there is a violation of terms and condition of insurance policy. It is further stated that accident did not take place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and it is the injured herself who is responsible for such accident and in any case there is contributory negligence on her part. 9. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 12.04.2019 by Predecessor of this Tribunal: 1. 10. Petitioner filed her examination in chief by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/1 on 24.12.2019. She relied upon copy of MLC as Ex. PW-1/1, original discharge summary as Ex. PW-1/2, copies of OPD cards as Mark-A , Medical Bills as Ex. PW-1/4, copy of Aadhar card and PAN card as Ex. PW- Smt. Roshan Aara vs Pushkar Hira on 25 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191802696/ 2 1/5 , DAR as Ex. PW-1/6 and OPD card issued from Sushruta Trauma Center as MACT No. 05/19 Smt. Roshan Aara v. Pushkar Hira Page No. 3 of 24 Ex.PW-1/7. Further, an additional affidavit was filed by petitioner in order to file disability certificate as Ex. PW-1/4 (colly). She was cross-examined on 24.12.2019 by learned counsel for insurance company as well as driver-cum- owner. Thereafter, she filed two additional affidavit of evidence relating to additional bill and disability certificate. 11. Such PW-1/ Victim/ Injured / Petitioner was cross examined by Ld. Counsel for insurance company/ respondent no.2. During cross examination, he deposed that he filed four bills no. 006/18/5-22 dated 15.12.2018, 02.11.2018,06.11.2018, and 21.11.2018 for Rs.948, Rs.778/-, Rs.525 and Rs.450 which are in the name of Aasaf Ali Khan. He denied the suggestion that accident took place due to his negligence and bills are not of accidental injuries. That he has not filed documentary evidence regarding his earning of Rs.10,000/- p.m. 12. An application of petitioner for leading additional evidence was allowed subject to that petitioner shall not be be entitled for interest from 02.03.2021 till the evidence led by her and i.e. 26.07.2022. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. 14. Respondent no.2/insurance company tendered evidence of Ms. Lalita Anand, Administrative Officer by way of affidavit as Ex.R-2W-1/A. She relied upon attested copy of insurance policy as Ex. R-2W-1/1, report of licence filed by IO as Ex. R-2W1/2, notice u/o 12 Rule 8 CPC as Ex.R-2W-1/3 and postal receipt as Ex. R-2W-1/4. That driver-cum-owner was holding a licence for LMV (non transport) whereas he was driving motorcycle at the time of accident and there is no endorsement for driving motorcycle. Further no MACT No. 05/19 Smt. Roshan Aara v. Pushkar Hira Page No. 4 of 24 evidence was led on behalf of driver-cum-owner. Hence RE was closed. Further, Ld. counsel for petitioner as well as respondent insurance company filed written arguments.
texts.arguments: 17. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. 18. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: MACT No. 05/19 Smt. Roshan Aara v. Pushkar Hira Page No. 5 of 24 Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. 18.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). It may be noted that in this background that in Cholamandlam Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD-Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of MACT No. 05/19 Smt. Roshan Aara v. Pushkar Hira Page No. 10 of 24 investigation and filing of chargesheet u/s 279/304 A IPC are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 3.Further in such case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar, the Hon'ble Supreme Court laid down a three step approach to decide compensation for the injured persons who have suffered permanent disability and same are as under: Injured = Rs. 5,08,860/- was 70 years old at the time of accident, hence multiplier of 5 is applicable (kindly see judgment of Rajkumar (Supra), para-11 r/w judgment of Sarla Verma v. DTC, para-40). Total Compensation Rs. 10,60,310/- MACT No. 05/19 Smt. Roshan Aara v. Pushkar Hira Pag Deduction, if any Nil Total Compensation after deduction Rs. 10,60,310/- Interest Simple interest @9% p.a from the date of filing Smt. Roshan Aara vs Pushkar Hira on 25 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191802696/ 10 DAR i.e. 07.01.2019 til actual realization of A amount/compensation. LIABILITY:- 33. 35. In the background of such fact proved on record by insurance company in this particular case and having regard to the ratio and direction by Hon'ble Supreme Court, three judges bench judgment of "National Insurance Company v. Swaran Singh ((2004) 3SCC 297)", the compensation will be MACT No. 05/19 Smt. Roshan Aara v. Pushkar Hira Page No. 17 of 24 payable in the first instance by the insurance company, but with liberty to recover the same from the driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle in question. 36. The award amount shall be deposited with State Bank of India, Saket Court Branch, New Delhi by way of RTGS/NEFT/IMPS in account of MACT FUND PARKING, A/c No. 35195787436, IFS Code SBIN0014244 and MICR code 110002342 under intimation to the Nazir along with calculation of interest and to the Counsel for the petitioner. 37. This court is in receipt of the orders dated 07.12.2018 passed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in FAO no. 842/2003 titled as Rajesh Tyagi & Ors. Vs. Jaibir Singh & Ors whereby the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has formulated MACAD(Motor Accident Claims Annunity Deposit Scheme) which has been made effective from 01.01.2019. The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is directed to disburse the amount in accordance with MACAD formulated by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. Smt. Roshan Aara vs Pushkar Hira on 25 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191802696/ 11 Apportionment:- 38. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". In the case of illiterate claimants, the Tribunal is allowed to consider the request for lumpsum payment for effecting purchase of any movable property such as agricultural implements, rickshaws etc. to earn a living. In the case of semi- illiterate claimants, the Tribunal should ordinarily invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. They are taking such a rigid and mechanical approach without understanding and appreciating the distinction drawn by this Court in the case of minors, illiterate claimants and Smt. Roshan Aara vs Pushkar Hira on 25 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191802696/ 12 widows and in the case of semiliterate and literate persons. Even in the case of literate persons, the Tribunals are automatically ordering investment of the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit without recording that having regard to the age or fiscal background or the strata of the MACT No. 05/19 Smt. Roshan Aara v. Pushkar Hira Page No. 20 of 24 society to which the claimant belongs or such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks it necessary to direct such investment in the larger interests of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded to him.
